inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average shares 5,140,565k from the H1 FY2026 interim EPS note 10(b) (basic 5,104,241k; convertible bonds fully retired, so dilution is share awards only). The CSV share column is back-calculated (net income / basic EPS) and is approximate; the filing's own diluted figure is used here. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and the US$40m/yr buyback programme (US$40.1m spent FY2024, US$40.1m FY2025, US$3.5m H1 FY2026) is the cash mechanism keeping the count flat.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash flow statement share-based compensation add-back (US$4.289m). No net-share-settlement tax withholding (EquityAwardTaxes = 0). Awards are satisfied by trustee market purchases (US$6.9m FY2025), so the forward SBC path is set at 0.25% of revenue, between the P&L expense and the trustee cash cost.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in USD (US$'000 in every annual and interim report; USD functional currency); HKEX quote in HKD. USD/HKD 7.8479 from Yahoo USDHKD=X at 2026-10-17T00:00Z (HKD peg band 7.75-7.85, so the rate is stable). Per-share values computed in USD then multiplied by 7.8479 to the HKD quote basis. Parity check (no dual listing): the interim declares basic EPS of HK16.1 cents against US 2.06 cents basic (105.05m / 5,104m), implying 7.82, within 0.4% of the rate used, confirming direction (USD -> HKD multiply).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD rate: 10-year UST ~4.3% + beta ~1.05 x 5.0% ERP = ~9.5% cost of equity. The company runs net cash (borrowings US$49.3m vs cash US$206.5m), so WACC = cost of equity = 9.5%. Freight-cycle risk is charged in the flows (mid-cycle margins, 25% bear weight), not as a WACC premium, and the same 9.5% is used in every scenario.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: FY2025 lease cash cost = principal US$37.2m + interest US$5.1m = US$42.3m = 2.0% of revenue, charged through lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (US$94.0m at 30 June 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is bank borrowings only (current + non-current). D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 total depreciation US$190.8m less ROU US$38.0m = US$152.8m = 7.3% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; flows are attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations. Pacific Basin is an operating company (owner-operator of ~106 owned Handysize/Supramax/Ultramax dry bulk vessels plus chartered-in tonnage), so it routes to the owner-FCF row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'; it is not an asset-holding vehicle, though the broker NAV is carried as a memo. CYCLICALITY: dry bulk earnings swing with the BHSI/BSI. EBITDA margin on revenue ran 12.6-14.5% in FY2018-20 and FY2023-25, 28.5-29.9% in the FY2021-22 boom, and 17.9% in H1 FY2026; the eight-year average is ~19% and the ex-boom average ~13.5%. The forward build therefore does NOT extrapolate any single year: FY2026 is set from the H1 run-rate, and from FY2027 margins revert to a through-cycle level (base 15.0%, which gives some weight to periodic booms without capitalising one). Revenue includes voyage costs (bunkers, port charges) so the margin is on gross revenue, not TCE. CAPEX: net of vessel disposal proceeds (gross capex FY2021-25 avg US$161m, disposal proceeds avg US$48m); the 10-vessel newbuild orderbook (capital commitments US$297.7m delivering to mid-2029) lifts base net capex to 6.5% of revenue FY2026-28 before settling at 6.0%. TAX: cash taxes are de minimis (US$0.6m FY2025) because international shipping income is largely exempt in HK and excluded from Pillar Two; 1% path. INTEREST INCOME stripped (US$11.1m) because net cash (US$157m) exceeds the owner-FCF base. BALANCE SHEET: net cash is at 30 June 2026 (cash and deposits US$206.5m less borrowings US$49.3m = US$157.2m, matching the company's stated net cash) while FY0 flows are FY2025; the H1 FY2026 cash build retained after dividends is ~US$23m (~HK$0.04/share) of overlap with year-1 flows, immaterial. NAV MEMO: broker market value of owned fleet US$2,070.6m vs book US$1,557.0m at 30 June 2026 gives adjusted NAV of ~US$2,396m = ~US$0.466/share = ~HK$3.66. SBC is small (0.2% of revenue), so the house/street band is narrow but not degenerate.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: through-cycle judgment (fleet growth plus freight inflation); trailing CAGRs are dominated by the FY2021-22 boom and its unwind
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.4% vs revenue 5yr 7.2% and EPS 3yr -56%: every trailing CAGR is a function of where the endpoints sit in the freight cycle (FY2020 trough, FY2022 peak, FY2025 trough-ish). None is a usable forward growth rate; the selected 2.5% is a through-cycle judgment. EPS 5yr CAGR undefined (FY2020 loss).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income. Owner-FCF CAGRs (-45.0% 3yr, 5.0% 5yr) are slightly below reported (-43.4%, 5.6%) because interest income rose with the net-cash position, not because SBC outgrew cash flow; SBC is ~US$4-7m/yr throughout.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands near H1 run-rate (revenue +9%, EBITDA margin 17%) on Red Sea / geopolitical tonne-mile inefficiency and firmer minor-bulk rates, then fades as Clarksons' forecast of supply outpacing demand in 2026-27 bites; margins settle at a 15% through-cycle level from FY2028.

bull.narrative: An ageing geared fleet and decarbonisation-driven scrapping (EEXI/CII, EU ETS) constrain Handysize/Supramax supply while minor-bulk demand holds; PB's outperformance vs BHSI/BSI and sub-US$6,800/day cash break-even let it earn an 18% through-cycle margin, and the newbuild programme is delivered into firm rates.

bear.narrative: Red Sea and other route inefficiencies unwind, newbuild deliveries (4.6% supply growth) outrun weak China steel/construction and tariff-hit minor-bulk trade, and rates revert to the FY2019/FY2024-25 pattern; margins sit at 12% with fleet renewal still costing 6.5% of revenue as dual-fuel regulation forces higher newbuild prices.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands near the H1 run-rate (revenue +9%, EBITDA margin 17%) on geopolitical tonne-mile inefficiency and firmer minor-bulk rates, then fades as supply growth outpaces demand in 2026-27 per Clarksons; EBITDA margin settles at a 15% through-cycle level from FY2028, net capex 6.5% of revenue while the 10-vessel orderbook delivers to mid-2029 then 6.0%. Value sits below the broker NAV (~HK$3.66), i.e. the market is paying roughly replacement value for the fleet.
scenario_narratives.bull: Supply discipline wins: an ageing geared fleet, decarbonisation-driven scrapping and limited newbuild yard slots keep Handysize/Supramax supply growth below minor-bulk demand. PB's premium over the BHSI/BSI indices (US$1,950-2,370/day in H1 2026) and sub-US$6,800/day cash break-even translate into an 18% through-cycle margin, and the newbuild programme is delivered into firm rates.
scenario_narratives.bear: Route inefficiencies unwind, newbuild deliveries outrun demand, and China steel/construction plus tariff-hit trade flows weaken minor-bulk volumes; rates revert to the FY2019/FY2024-25 pattern. Margins sit at 12% while fleet renewal still costs 6.5% of revenue as dual-fuel regulation lifts newbuild prices.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because this is a pure freight-rate cyclical and the company's own outlook cites supply outpacing demand in 2026; bull cut from 35% to 25% because the bull case needs supply discipline, demand resilience and continued index outperformance together; base 50% is the through-cycle reversion. The net-cash balance sheet removes solvency risk, so bear is not raised further.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF for a dry bulk owner-operator. The latest year is never the base: margins revert to a through-cycle 15% after FY2026, capex is net of vessel sales and includes the committed newbuild programme, and a 12x terminal cap reflects cyclicality. The broker NAV is the cross-check: when the DCF sits below NAV the market is pricing ships at replacement cost rather than on their earnings power.
key_risks_to_valuation: Freight rates (BHSI/BSI) are the dominant driver; a 1pp change in through-cycle EBITDA margin moves value by roughly 10%.
Geopolitical route inefficiencies (Red Sea, Panama) flatter 2026 tonne-miles and could unwind quickly.
Decarbonisation regulation (IMO net-zero framework, EU ETS) could force earlier fleet renewal at higher newbuild prices.
Share count is the filing's diluted weighted average; the CSV share column is back-calculated and approximate.
Fleet market values are broker estimates and move with the cycle; NAV memo is not a floor.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2.23-4.45 HKD. FX from Yahoo USDHKD=X.
data_sources.financials: Pacific Basin annual reports FY2018-FY2025 and interim reports H1 2024-H1 2026 (US$'000), via 2343.HK_Metrics.csv and kpis; diluted shares, net cash, fleet market value and capital commitments from the 2026 interim report.
data_sources.qualitative: 2026 interim report outlook and business highlights; Clarksons Research supply/demand forecasts as quoted by the company.
